decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i0 dossier: NL3 contract, exact transition and event bindings, source transition tr_0001, closed transition line 19, and reachability facts.
decisions.reason: The clause says that on power on the system turns into HumanDrivingMode. The exact bound transition line 19 carries Power_On and targets HumanDrivingMode, but the supplied finite verification and inspection facts state that this transition is unreachable from top-level initial entry. The possible narrower reading that endpoint and trigger presence alone suffice is excluded by the candidate's explicit requirement for a reachable transition from the system initial scope.
decisions.violated_obligation: A reachable Power_On transition from the system initial scope must enter HumanDrivingMode; the exact transition exists but is not reachable from top-level initial entry.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i10 dossier: NL5 termination contract, exact FinalState binding, finite reachability and outgoing-transition facts, formal terminal-edge inventory, and completed V4 receipt.
decisions.reason: The clause requires that after Power Off the system reaches final state with completion semantics. The exact bound state FinalState is reachable, non-final, and has no outgoing transitions; the supplied formal facts provide no terminal edge or explicit terminal fact. V4 independently checks the exact stable leaf and finds no committed successor. An intentional-terminal reading is not supported by the state name or by zero outgoing transitions, and the supplied continuation/progress contract excludes treating this non-final reachable leaf as acceptable completion.
decisions.violated_obligation: The reachable non-final FinalState must provide continuation or explicit stable completion semantics; the supplied facts instead establish a reachable non-final leaf without a formal terminal edge.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i11 dossier: NL3 derived initial-entry contract, unresolved empty model binding, and deterministic owner-initial-entry frontier result.
decisions.reason: The clause requires an unconditional default entry from the system root to HumanDrivingMode. The supplied deterministic result explicitly retains the owner-initial-entry check as unresolved, and the binding is empty and imprecise. No exact owner or target identity is supplied for deciding whether the required root entry exists or is malformed. A later exact binding could decide the issue, but that possibility is not evidence for either reading.
decisions.violated_obligation: The system root must have an unconditional default entry to the authored operating state HumanDrivingMode; the supplied dossier cannot decide this without an exact owner and target binding.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i12 dossier: UML initial-pseudostate invariant, exact transition line 19 binding, native trigger fact, and completed S3 receipt.
decisions.reason: The supplied invariant requires the exact outgoing initial-pseudostate transition line 19 to have neither trigger nor guard. The native closed-model fact identifies line 19 as that initial transition and reports the trigger Power_On; the S3 receipt compares the expected empty trigger set with the observed Power_On set and reports a mismatch. An ordinary transition elsewhere cannot rebut the invariant because the exact carrier is bound as the initial transition.
decisions.violated_obligation: Initial transition line 19 must have neither trigger nor guard; the exact native transition has the Power_On trigger.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i13 dossier: UML initial-pseudostate invariant, exact transition line 21 binding, native trigger fact, and completed S3 receipt.
decisions.reason: The supplied invariant requires the exact outgoing initial-pseudostate transition line 21 to have neither trigger nor guard. The native closed-model fact identifies line 21 as that initial transition and reports the trigger Power_Off; the S3 receipt compares the expected empty trigger set with the observed Power_Off set and reports a mismatch. An ordinary transition elsewhere cannot rebut the invariant because the exact carrier is bound as the initial transition.
decisions.violated_obligation: Initial transition line 21 must have neither trigger nor guard; the exact native transition has the Power_Off trigger.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i2 dossier: NL4.2 contract, exact AutoFinal consumer and outer transition bindings, source transition tr_0005, and closed-model endpoint facts.
decisions.reason: The clause requires the human-steering-and-brake stimulus in AutoFinal to transition to HumanDrivingMode. The exact AutoFinal consumer exits to the completion pseudostate and writes R45RouteToken = 5; a separate guarded transition from AutonomousMode targets HumanDrivingMode. This establishes a first reading that the exact AutoFinal consumer does not have the required endpoint. However, the supplied source and model facts also support a competent macro-lowering reading in which the child exit and guarded outer transition jointly implement the authored cross-scope transition. The closure provides no complete macro-equivalence certificate to resolve these compatible readings.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The authored cross-scope transition may be implemented by the exact AutoFinal exit transition line 15 together with the guarded outer transition line 18, as represented by source transition tr_0005.
decisions.violated_obligation: Within AutoFinal, the human steering and brake stimulus must result in a transition to HumanDrivingMode.

decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i3 dossier: NL5 endpoint contract, exact source/target/event/transition bindings, reachability facts, and completed S2 receipt.
decisions.reason: The clause requires a reachable Power_Off transition from the system scope into FinalState. decisions.basis: Obligation 0000:r2:i4 dossier: NL5 termination contract, exact FinalState source/model facts, reachable-leaf diagnostic, and absence of a formal completion edge.
decisions.reason: The clause requires stable termination after Power Off reaches FinalState. This supports a first reading that stable completion is not established. The dossier therefore leaves the semantic boundary between dead end and intended terminal state open.
decisions.strongest_defeater: FinalState may be intended as a terminal convention based on the exact source state and its zero-outgoing topology, although no formal terminal marker is supplied.
decisions.violated_obligation: After Power Off reaches FinalState, the system must stably terminate there with explicit completion semantics.

issues.basis: NL3 contract; source transition tr_0001; closed transition line 19; inspection event-consumer fact for Power_On; finite verification refutation for initial-entry transition line 19.
issues.expected: A reachable Power On transition from the system initial scope must enter HumanDrivingMode.
issues.observed: The closed transition line 19 targets HumanDrivingMode and carries Power_On, but is unreachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The required Power On initial transition to HumanDrivingMode exists, but the complete closed-model facts mark its exact carrier transition as unreachable from a top-level initial entry. This preserves the endpoint property while identifying the operational contrast.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint and trigger are exact and present; only operational reachability of the initial transition is contradicted by the supplied deterministic facts.
issues.title: Power-on entry is not reachable

issues.basis: NL4 contract; source transition tr_0004; closed transition line 20; inspection transition fact showing trigger front_distance_10 and guard null.
issues.expected: A transition to AutonomousMode selected by guard front_distance > 10 must exist.
issues.observed: The closed HumanDrivingMode-to-AutonomousMode transition is triggered by front_distance_10 and has no guard.
issues.reason: The endpoint exists with the exact target and front-distance event, but the NL contract requires the front-distance condition as the selecting guard. The closed transition has an event trigger and no parsed guard, so the endpoint alone does not satisfy the guarded transition property.
issues.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The FCSTM event is named for the same front-distance expression, so the supplied facts do not establish whether event and guard semantics are behaviorally equivalent; the precise guarded endpoint distinction remains the issue.
issues.title: Autonomous transition trigger is modeled as an event

issues.basis: NL4.2 contract; source transition tr_0005; closed AutoFinal transition line 15 to [*]; closed outer transition line 18 guarded by R45RouteToken == 5; source trace macro root mapping.
issues.expected: Within the AutoFinal context, the human steering and brake stimulus must transition to HumanDrivingMode.
issues.observed: The exact AutoFinal consumer exits to [*] and writes R45RouteToken = 5; a separate guarded AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode transition performs the outer target transfer.
issues.reason: The exact AutoFinal consumer transition responds to the required event by exiting to the composite completion pseudostate, while the authored semantic target is HumanDrivingMode. The outer AutonomousMode transition reaches HumanDrivingMode only when its route variable guard is satisfied; the closure does not establish this as a direct AutoFinal-to-HumanDrivingMode transition.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The protected macro composition may intentionally implement the authored cross-scope transition through a child exit and guarded outer transition; the supplied closure does not provide a complete macro-equivalence certificate for this join.
issues.title: Auto-final response reaches the outer exit but lacks a direct endpoint

issues.basis: NL5 endpoint contract; source transition tr_0006; closed transition line 21; inspection Power_Off consumer fact; finite verification refutation for initial-entry transition line 21.
issues.expected: A reachable Power Off transition from the system scope must enter FinalState.
issues.observed: The closed transition line 21 carries Power_Off and targets FinalState, but is unreachable from top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The required Power Off transition to FinalState exists, but the complete finite and inspection facts mark its exact initial transition carrier unreachable from a top-level initial entry. The endpoint remains present; the contrast is operational reachability of the completion edge.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint and trigger are exact and present; the supplied negative fact concerns only reachability, while this atomic contract is typed as an endpoint obligation.
issues.title: Power-off completion transition is unreachable

issues.basis: NL5 termination contract; exact FinalState source/model binding; inspection LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING diagnostic; finite verification deadlock refutation for FinalState.
issues.expected: After Power Off reaches FinalState, the system must terminate there with stable completion semantics.
issues.observed: FinalState is reachable but has zero outgoing transitions, and no supplied explicit completion edge closes its parent scope.
issues.reason: FinalState is reachable and has no outgoing transition, while the supplied termination contract requires stable termination at that target. The closed topology leaves the terminal state as a leaf without an owner-completion edge, so the termination semantics are not fully closed.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A leaf named FinalState may be intended as a terminal state in the target formalism, but the supplied facts provide no explicit formal terminal marker or completion semantics beyond the state name.
issues.title: Final state does not close its owning scope

issues.basis: NL3 source transition tr_0001; FCSTM transition:line:19 targets state:HumanDrivingMode:line:8 and triggers Power_On, while inspection and finite verification facts mark that consumer unreachable from initial entry.
issues.expected: A Power On-triggered transition from the system's top-level initial context must enter HumanDrivingMode.
issues.observed: The exact Power On transition targets HumanDrivingMode and is declared, but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty and reachable_from_initial is false for transition:line:19.
issues.reason: The required Power On transition to HumanDrivingMode exists with the expected target and trigger, but its root initial carrier is not reachable from a top-level initial entry. This is a behavioral consequence of the conditional initial-entry topology, not an endpoint mismatch.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The endpoint and trigger are exact, so the issue depends on interpreting the NL endpoint obligation as requiring an operationally reachable transition; if endpoint existence alone is intended, the closed transition satisfies that narrower property.
issues.title: Power-on entry is operationally unreachable

issues.basis: NL4 contract source hint is 'unresolved source'; source transition tr_0004 and FCSTM transition:line:20 provide a possible observed relation but do not authorize rewriting the source contract.
issues.expected: A transition selected by front_distance > 10 must enter AutonomousMode.
issues.observed: The closed model has a front_distance_10-triggered transition from HumanDrivingMode to AutonomousMode, but the normative source remains unresolved.
issues.reason: The target AutonomousMode and the front-distance event are exact, but the contract's source is explicitly unresolved. The closed model contains HumanDrivingMode to AutonomousMode, yet source identity cannot be completed from the supplied contract without converting the observed source into the normative source.
issues.requirement_quote: when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source artifact's unique front-distance transition is HumanDrivingMode to AutonomousMode, which may be the intended source if a later binding stage is permitted to resolve the open source from the author diagram.
issues.title: Autonomous transition source remains unresolved

issues.basis: NL4.2 source transition tr_0005; AutoFinal consumer transition:line:15 targets [*], while transition:line:18 supplies the final HumanDrivingMode target under guard R45RouteToken == 5.
issues.expected: Within the AutoFinal scope, the human-steering-and-brake stimulus must transition to HumanDrivingMode.
issues.observed: The stimulus from AutoFinal reaches the AutonomousMode completion pseudostate with effect R45RouteToken = 5; a separate guarded transition from AutonomousMode reaches HumanDrivingMode.
issues.reason: The required event and target are represented, but the exact AutoFinal consumer exits to the AutonomousMode completion pseudostate and relies on a separate guarded AutonomousMode-to-HumanDrivingMode transition. The closed model therefore does not contain one exact transition directly from AutoFinal to HumanDrivingMode carrying the complete requested relation.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The protected author transition tr_0005 is lowered into a composite exit plus route-control transition, so the whole macro may implement the requested endpoint if the downstream macro closure accepts that lowering.
issues.title: Auto-final response endpoint is scoped through a composite exit

issues.basis: NL5 source transition tr_0006; FCSTM transition:line:21 targets state:FinalState:line:17 with trigger Power_Off, while inspection and finite verification facts mark the consumer unreachable.
issues.expected: A Power Off-triggered transition from the system must enter FinalState operationally.
issues.observed: The Power Off transition exists and targets FinalState, but transition:line:21 has reachable_from_initial false and Power_Off has no reachable consumer transition.
issues.reason: The exact Power Off transition targets FinalState and carries the expected trigger, but its consumer is unreachable from a top-level initial entry. Endpoint existence alone does not establish that the required completion response can occur in the reachable operating graph.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The requested endpoint and trigger are present exactly; if the contract is structural endpoint existence rather than reachable response behavior, the endpoint is satisfied.
issues.title: Power-off final-state consumer is unreachable

issues.basis: NL5 termination contract; FinalState exact model ref state:FinalState:line:17; inspection diagnostic LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING and refuted deadlock check both report zero outgoing transitions.
issues.expected: After Power Off reaches FinalState, the system must stably terminate at that state without requiring further continuation.
issues.observed: FinalState is reachable and has no outgoing transition; the supplied facts do not provide a formal completion marker or a proof that this leaf is a stable terminal state, so the termination property is not expressible by the frozen registry.
issues.reason: FinalState is the exact termination target and is reachable, but the supplied inspection and verification facts report that the reachable leaf has no outgoing transition. The finite deadlock-frontier fact does not establish stable termination for a termination contract; it is a distinct unsupported completion consequence requiring a precise non-frozen predicate claim.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A leaf with no outgoing transitions may itself be the intended terminal convention, and the source explicitly calls it FinalState; absent a formal completion marker, the supplied facts do not uniquely distinguish stable termination from a dead-end.
issues.title: Final state does not provide stable completion
